_why: The standard sub-headers that repeat inside every component folder. Zach proposed the idea and five of the aspects (click, hover, drag, visual appearance, adding members); the rest were DERIVED by classifying all 468 backlog items until coverage stopped improving. Coverage: 438/468 = 94%, median 2 aspects per item. The 30 that do not fit are system-scope, not component-scope, and belong in a separate SYSTEM bucket.
_method: docs/build_architecture_proposal.py sibling analysis; keyword classification over name+whatItDoes+area. NOTE: this is a VOCABULARY derivation, not an item classifier — 60% of items match more than one aspect, so counts are indicative of which aspects earn their place, not of a final assignment.

INTERACTION._what: what a person DOES to the component. Lives in components/<Name>/ — the handlers.

MODEL._what: what the component IS and how it is drawn. Mostly scene/ (pure) plus the shape's own geometry.

CHROME._what: the editor surfaces that reach the component. Each entry point is ONE call into scene/.

examples: The whole whiteboard is a System, and you are always inside one
CAD exporter maps hardware to components
Standard drop-in components: Data Recorders, Visualizers, Loggers
Obsidian plugin, in the same repo
uncovered_system_scope._verdict: Not features OF a component. They need a system-level home or an explicit out-of-scope ruling.
